comparison: Both evaluate implications and recommendations (C2, C72-C77) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes these claims are speculative and require empirical validation. Peer reviewers similarly express concern that global patterns obscure local cultural variation, suggesting implications may be overstated. Strong agreement on the uncertain nature of policy recommendations.

Both evaluate sampling methodology and data collection (C3, C30-C35, C83-C87) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval praises the justified sampling approach and clear presentation. Peer reviewers explicitly commended the 'carefully collected dataset' and methodology. Peer review also includes outcome variable operationalization (C88-C92) which OpenEval evaluates separately in R6. Strong agreement on methodological quality.

Both evaluate statistical practices and model validation (C106-C111) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights conservative alpha, effect size emphasis, and diagnostic procedures as sound methodology. Peer reviewers praised analytical rigor and use of 'standard and widely used tools.' Complete agreement on statistical quality, though OpenEval provides more detailed technical assessment.

Both evaluate core regression and variance partitioning results (C4, C39-C44) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate modeling and clear quantification of predictor contributions. Peer reviewers explicitly affirmed findings showing 'detailed links between societal and academic interest.' Strong agreement, though OpenEval addresses broader claim set including C37-C38, C45, and C5-C10.

Both evaluate findings on factors differentiating scientific vs. societal interest (C11-C12) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on Wikipedia-specific effects. Peer review groups these with aesthetic factors (C68, C70-C71) and accepts the distinction between interest types. Agreement on support, though peer review takes broader view of related claims.

Both evaluate colorfulness and phylogenetic proximity findings (C68-C71) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate citations and well-grounded interpretation linking to aesthetic value. Peer reviewers accepted these findings as part of demonstrating links between interest types. Complete agreement, with OpenEval providing more detailed assessment of inferential reasoning.

Both address taxon-specific findings for Tracheophyta. OpenEval evaluates C50 (post-hoc explanation) as UNCERTAIN, noting it's speculative without direct evidence. Peer review evaluates C49-C50 together as SUPPORTED, accepting the finding and explanation as part of 'compelling analyses.' Disagreement: OpenEval more critical of mechanistic interpretation.

Both evaluate taxon-specific differential effects (C49, C61) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes Figure 4 results and within-group heterogeneity. Peer review groups C61 with body size findings (C8-C10, C57) and accepts as part of nuanced analysis. Agreement on support, though peer review addresses broader claim set.

Both address alignment between scientific and societal interest. OpenEval evaluates C13, C36 as SUPPORTED based on residual analysis. Peer review evaluates C13, C37-C38 as SUPPORTED, praising model performance and interpretation. Agreement on support, with overlapping focus on C13 but different complementary claims.

Both address common names predicting interest (C53). OpenEval evaluates C53-C56 as SUPPORTED while transparently acknowledging methodological limitations. Peer review evaluates C53 with utilitarian factors (C5-C7, C45) as SUPPORTED without questioning limitations. Agreement on support, though OpenEval more critical of interpretive challenges.

Both address body size findings (C57-C60). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED with mechanistic interpretation contextualized in literature. Peer review groups C57 with taxon-specific effects (C8-C10, C61) as SUPPORTED without challenging interpretation. Complete agreement on support.

Both evaluate operationalization of outcome variables (C88-C92). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations and justified methodological choices. Peer review includes these claims within broader methodological evaluation as SUPPORTED. Complete agreement, though peer review addresses larger claim set including sampling methodology.

Both address normative recommendations. OpenEval evaluates C77, C82 as UNCERTAIN, noting they are prescriptive without empirical testing. Peer review includes C77 with broader implications (C2, C25, C72-C76) as UNCERTAIN due to cultural variation concerns. Agreement on uncertain status, though different specific concerns.

OpenEval evaluates range size findings (C62-C63, C101-C102) as SUPPORTED with dual interpretation of commonness and accessibility. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific claims.

OpenEval evaluates taxonomic uniqueness findings (C64-C65, C99-C100) as SUPPORTED, noting statistical clarity but inferential mechanistic interpretations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific claims.

OpenEval evaluates IUCN listing findings (C66-C67) as SUPPORTED while acknowledging circularity problem and ambiguous causal direction. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific claims.

OpenEval evaluates literature review and motivation claims (C1, C17-C21, C27-C29) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations establishing knowledge gap. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific background claims.

OpenEval evaluates contextual framing claims (C14-C16, C78-C81) as SUPPORTED, connecting attention patterns to cultural values and conservation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific framing claims.

OpenEval evaluates literature synthesis on factors affecting species attention (C22-C26, C46-C48, C51-C52, C56, C93-C105) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer review R8 touches on C25 regarding cultural variability but doesn't systematically evaluate this literature synthesis.

Peer review evaluates utilitarian factors driving attention (C5-C7, C45, C53) as SUPPORTED, noting work 'reveals biases.' OpenEval addresses these claims across multiple results (R2 for C5-C7, C45; R7 for C53) rather than as unified evaluation.
